title: PR's own motion measurements are arithmetically impossible: 3×30.6px vs 14×11.2px over the same 24 frames
detail: Same 24 timestamps, same deterministic sim: BEFORE total = 3×30.6 ≈ 92px, AFTER total = 14×11.2 ≈ 157px. Render-behind lag bounds the difference at ~one tick (~31px). Both summaries cannot be correct.
recommended_fix: Re-run tools/measure_packet_motion.py on fresh strips and paste the unedited output; reconcile holds/moving counts and means so totals match within one tick.

title: measure_packet_motion.py counts a lost packet track as a 'hold', silently inflating the headline metric
evidence:
+            c = live_centroid(os.path.join(d, f), xmax=xmax)
+            if prev and c:
+                disp = ((c[0] - prev[0]) ** 2 + (c[1] - prev[1]) ** 2) ** 0.5
+            else:
+                disp = 0.0
+            rows.append((f, disp))
...
+    b_holds = sum(1 for _, d in before if d < 0.5)
detail: When no exact-color cluster is found (c is None), displacement records 0.0 and counts as a hold. A lost track is indistinguishable from a stationary packet in the PR-evidence metric.
recommended_fix: Track found/lost per frame; exclude lost frames from holds (or report them separately) instead of recording disp = 0.0.

title: demos/motion.dem claims the strip window has 'no arrivals', but the PR's own data says 10 of 24 AFTER frames are post-arrival
evidence:
+# takes 8 ticks/edge = 400 ms: the packet crosses edge0 from ~t42 to ~t50,
+# so the strip window 2200..2600 ms is a pure mid-edge glide, no hops, no
+# arrivals — the displacement delta (steps vs glide) reads unmixed.
[vs pr-body]
+holds (<0.5px): BEFORE=21/24  AFTER=10/24 (post-arrival)
detail: t50 = 2500ms; the window runs to 2600ms, so ~100ms is post-arrival by the demo's own timeline, and the PR annotates 10 frames '(post-arrival)'. The comment misdescribes the measurement scene.
recommended_fix: Fix the motion.dem comment (window includes arrival), or narrow the strip window to end before ~2500ms if a pure mid-edge read is intended.

title: Trail ring shift path hardcodes capacity 3 (trail[2]) while the append path is length-generic
detail: Echo capacity 3 is restated in three places; changing TRAIL_FADES or the array size without editing trail[2] silently drops the newest echo or misaligns fades.
recommended_fix: Use trail[len(trail)-1] = {dwx, dwy} (or a named ECHO_N constant) so the shift path derives capacity like the append path does.

title: motion-strip silently ignores a 6th argument that isn't the literal 'snapshot'
detail: A typo'd mode argument (e.g. 'snapshott') is accepted and quietly runs interp mode, producing the opposite evidence strip of what was asked for.
recommended_fix: Validate rest[5] when present: if len(rest) == 6 && rest[5] != "snapshot" { usage(); os.exit(2) }.

evidence:

detail: Guard checks only b_steps; empty a_steps crashes. zip drops extra frames silently when the two strip dirs differ, misaligning the printed before/after table.
recommended_fix: Guard a_steps separately; assert len(before) == len(after) (or pad/report) before zipping.

title: render_strip_frame's `cat` parameter is never used
evidence:
+render_strip_frame :: proc(
+	rc: ^Render_Ctx,
+	state: ^pp.Run_State,
+	cat: ^pp.Catalogs,
+	outdir, demo_name: string,
+	ms: i64,
+	sim_tick: u64,
+	alpha: f32,
+	frames: ^int,
+) {
+	img := capture_frame(rc, &state.topology, &state.bundles, &state.flow, &state.crisis, &state.health,
+		state.health_enabled, sim_tick, state.era, state.seed, nil, alpha)
+	path := fmt.tprintf("%s/%s-%06dms.png", outdir, demo_name, ms)
+	rl.ExportImage(img, strings.clone_to_cstring(path, context.temp_allocator))
+	rl.UnloadImage(img)
+	frames^ += 1
+}
detail: The body never reads `cat`; the parameter is dead weight and misleads readers into thinking the render depends on the catalogs.
recommended_fix: Drop the `cat` parameter from render_strip_frame and update its single call site.
